name: Cap'n Jazz
label: Jade Tree
lede: Suburban Chicago teenagers with a French horn, an a-ha cover and a 28-word album title broke up in Little Rock in 1995, and nearly every band that came out of the wreckage became someone's favorite.

eras.title: Toe Jam in Buffalo Grove
eras.text: Cap'n Jazz started as a suburban kids' band: two brothers and two friends in Buffalo Grove, Illinois, northwest of Chicago, working out their own version of Gauge and Fugazi.

years.h: Tim and Mike Kinsella start Toe Jam in Buffalo Grove, Illinois
years.p: [[Tim Kinsella|0350b5ce-ab77-4cbf-a550-944b851e4454]], 14 or 15, and his little brother [[Mike Kinsella|2b5e086f-cb7b-4f92-8a85-6a1c38ceb598]] form Toe Jam with guitarist [[Victor Villarreal|2758e65d-226a-4f21-b1e2-1eb72c4300b1]] and bassist [[Sam Zurick|5a8b6d87-8e75-42a5-9a70-c03e84b22b67]]. They soon become Cap'n Jazz.
years.xp: Mike Kinsella took over the drums at 12, after the original drummer quit to concentrate on football. He learned on a 16-piece kit.

eras.title: Five kids and the longest title in emo
eras.text: With Davey von Bohlen added on second guitar, Cap'n Jazz made singles, compilation tracks and one album whose title runs to 28 words. By the time the album mattered, the band was already over.

years.h: First Cap'n Jazz records: a Further Beyond comp and an Underdog 7-inch
years.p: Cap'n Jazz appears on the Further Beyond compilation Boys 16 to 18 Years... Age of Action and releases the Sometimes if you stand further away from something... 7-inch on Underdog Records.

years.h: Davey von Bohlen joins on guitar and backing vocals
years.p: [[Davey von Bohlen|b1bb1a6c-898b-4d0d-ab0a-6473859d229b]] completes the classic five-piece Cap'n Jazz line-up.

years.h: Shmap'n Shmazz · Man With Gun, a 28-word real title
years.p: Cap'n Jazz's only album is officially titled Burritos, Inspiration Point, Fork Balloon Sports, Cards in the Spokes, Automatic Biographies, Kites, Kung Fu, Trophies, Banana Peels We've Slipped On and Egg Shells We've Tippy Toed Over. The CD shortened it to Shmap'n Shmazz.

years.h: Cap'n Jazz breaks up on tour after a show in Little Rock
years.p: Nine days into a summer tour, Cap'n Jazz splits after a show at Das Yutes a Go-Go in Little Rock, Arkansas. Davey von Bohlen goes home to [[The Promise Ring|63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565]] full-time.
years.xp: Tim Kinsella's Wikipedia entry dates the final show to July 14, 1995. Analphabetapolothology later included two songs recorded at the band's last show, Forget Who We Are and Olerud.

years.h: Tim Kinsella starts Joan of Arc the same year
years.p: Out of the wreckage [[Tim Kinsella|0350b5ce-ab77-4cbf-a550-944b851e4454]] forms [[Joan of Arc|0f2fea44-7e03-47f9-86e6-91d0a22fd0ee]], the band he would lead for the next 25 years.

eras.title: Scattered, then anthologized
eras.text: Cap'n Jazz got bigger after it ended. Its members went on to Joan of Arc, The Promise Ring and American Football, and a Jade Tree double CD put the whole catalog in front of people who had never seen them play.

years.p: [[Mike Kinsella|2b5e086f-cb7b-4f92-8a85-6a1c38ceb598]] starts [[American Football|4ebb5ad3-9018-407d-8c24-c03011ab9ac6]] with Steve Lamos and Steve Holmes. Its one 1999 album became a cornerstone of the same scene.

q: Weeks later I realized I named it wrong.
years.h: Analphabetapolothology: all of Cap'n Jazz on two Jade Tree CDs
years.p: Ninety-nine minutes: the album, the singles, comp tracks, demos, an [[a-ha|7364dea6-ca9a-48e3-be01-b44ad0d19897]] Take On Me cover and a take on Ooh Do I Love You. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.
years.xp: Tim Kinsella came up with the title, drove to Madison, Wisconsin, and typed it in. He noticed the mistake after it was printed. The liner guide says to read it as an alphabet apolo(tholo)gy.

years.h: Owls: Cap'n Jazz minus Davey von Bohlen
years.p: The Kinsella brothers, Victor Villarreal and Sam Zurick sign to Jade Tree as [[Owls|f505c9ad-0298-46d5-ada6-c4e88b145ae2]] on May 3, 2001, and release an album recorded with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The band lasted one tour.

eras.title: The reunion nobody expected
eras.text: Fifteen years after Little Rock, Cap'n Jazz played again, first as a surprise and then on festival stages. They came back again in 2017 and 2024, the last time for the album's 30th anniversary.

years.h: A surprise Cap'n Jazz set at Joan of Arc's variety show
years.p: Cap'n Jazz plays an impromptu set at the Empty Bottle in Chicago during Joan of Arc's Don't Mind Control Variety Show.

years.h: Cap'n Jazz's first official reunion show: Forecastle Festival
years.p: The five-piece plays Forecastle in Louisville, Kentucky. The hometown show at Chicago's Bottom Lounge sells out in 48 hours, so they add a second night.
years.xp: The Chicago shows marked a vinyl reissue of Analphabetapolothology. More US dates followed that summer and fall.

years.h: Nate Kinsella replaces Davey von Bohlen for FYF and Riot Fest
years.p: Cousin [[Nate Kinsella|dee29ad9-ba52-4af1-8372-4acbfb725554]] takes the second guitar for shows at FYF Fest in Los Angeles, Riot Fest in Chicago, and dates in San Francisco, New York and London.

years.h: Back at the Empty Bottle, then Las Vegas
years.p: Cap'n Jazz reunites at the Empty Bottle in Chicago and five days later plays Best Friends Forever Fest in Las Vegas.

years.h: 30 years of Shmap'n Shmazz, sold out in San Francisco
years.p: On an anniversary tour with Coffin Prick, Cap'n Jazz sells out the Great American Music Hall. One review noticed fans young enough to be Tim Kinsella's kids.
